messages:
alex (AE): Heads up — POC kickoff with GraniteHealth tomorrow 9am PT. They're gating on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, RBAC mappings, and domain ownership proof. Also asked for pricing for a Dedicated trial during the POC and our security questionnaire answers. @sam can you join?

sam (Solutions Eng): Yep I can. Quick checklist needed from them: IdP metadata (SAML), SCIM spec (they said delta sync + bulk import), RBAC mapping doc (group -> role), and expected user counts. Also they mentioned SCIM rate limits and retry semantics.

maria (SE): For pricing, do we have a standard POC Dedicated tier or do we need a custom commit? I can propose a 2-GPU trial with a usage cap and timeboxed credits. @finance FYI.

leo (Security): On the questionnaire: we can share SOC2 Type II pdf and a high-level pen-test summary. We don't share KMS/HSM configs but can describe KMS integrations. Need to confirm data residency — they prefer EU.

danielle (Sales): Their legal team flagged domain-proofing and admin provisioning: they want automatic domain lock and delegation for admins. Also asked whether we support Okta SCIM bulk import for on-boarding ~50k users. That's a hard stop for them.

alex (AE): Action items: @sam produce a single-page SAML + SCIM runbook and a sample RBAC mapping; @leo assemble the security pack (SOC2 + a short answers doc); @maria confirm Dedicated POC pricing + limits; @ops-bot please create a kickoff invite. I'll coordinate legal questions.

ops-bot: Created calendar event — "GraniteHealth POC Kickoff" — 2025-06-18 16:00 UTC. RSVP: alex (AE), danielle (Sales), sam (Solutions Eng), maria (SE), leo (Security). Link: https://cal.example/evt/GRN-POC

sam (Solutions Eng): SCIM/Rate guidance snippet we can share:
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/{id}
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Rate-Limit: 600/min per org (default)
Retry-After: 120s on 429
Bulk: POST /scim/v2/Bulk with chunk size <= 2500 users
```

maria (SE): Note: bulk import is supported via our async import job — needs a 24h lead to provision staging import bucket. I'll add that to the runbook.

danielle (Sales): For domain proofing, do we accept DNS TXT or file-hosted verification? Which is faster for them?

sam (Solutions Eng): We support DNS TXT and SAML entityID verification. DNS TXT is usually faster for infra teams; file upload works for some customers but DNS is preferred for automation.

leo (Security): Also add a note for legal: Dedicated POC will have our standard SLOs but we recommend a canary fallback for auth services and an SLA doc for the trial. I'll write a one-paragraph summary.

alex (AE): Great — I'll compile everything into a single presales pack and send to GraniteHealth by EOD. If anyone sees a blocker (especially on EU residency / data flow), ping me ASAP. :thumbsup:
